newsitem.title: UK: GEC wins 2 bln stg nuclear submarine order.
newsitem.headline: GEC wins 2 bln stg nuclear submarine order.

text.p: The British government said on Monday that it has awarded General Electric Co Plc's GEC-Marconi a 2.0 billion pounds ($3.2 billion) contract to build three nuclear powered hunter-killer submarines for the Royal Navy.

Defence procurement minister James Arbuthnot told parliament that the Astute Class submarines, previously called Trafalgar Class, would be built at GEC-Marconi's VSEL Barrow yard in northwest England and would "help sustain around 7,000 jobs."

Arbuthnot said the new boats were expected to enter service early in the next century. They will be powered by Rolls-Royce PWR2 pressurised water nuclear reactors and armed with Spearfish torpedoes and Harpoon anti-ship missiles as well as conventionally-armed Tomahawk cruise missiles.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) selected GEC in December 1995, in preference to VSEL itself for the prime contracting job but the final contract was made subject to agreement on the all-in price for design, construction and certain in-service costs, including a refit.

GEC took over VSEL in 1995, after outbidding British Aerospace Plc for the shipbuilder. As Britain's only submarine yard, VSEL was always expected to win the main construction contract for the Trafalgar work, even if it lost the competition for the primary role.

"It was still necessary to negotiate an acceptable price, and while this has taken some time, the result is a taut contract giving excellent value-for-money to the taxpayer," the MoD said in a statement on Monday. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
